To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
navigation impairments are a reliable early cognitive marker of conversion to Alzheimer's disease dementia in patients with mild cognitive impairments.
the neural networks involved in navigation are affected by normal aging and AD.

the neural network of spatial navigation is affected differently in normal aging and AD, and the navigation abilities of MCI patients are differentially affected depending on the cognitive profiles of these patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the neural mechanisms that underlie navigation deficits, and how these deficits are associated with different cognitive profiles in normal aging and MCI

understanding how navigation abilities are altered in the prodromal stages of neurodegenerative disorders, with particular reference to AD, and with determining whether these deficits can be used as early diagnostic markers of AD dementia.
the study of the neural basis of spatial navigation in normal aging, mild AD, and MCI, and its possible use as an early cognitive marker for AD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
navigation deficits are associated with different brain alterations, depending on the stage and type of dementia, but they can be used as early markers of cognitive decline.
the navigation deficits in MCI are more similar to those in AD than in normal aging, but the pattern of brain activation during spatial navigation is more similar to that in normal aging than in AD.
the neural network of navigational processing is affected in both normal aging and the early stages of AD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
navigation deficits are not a unique feature of AD dementia but are also found in other neurodegenerations and in normal aging.
navigation deficits may provide useful information to distinguish patients at higher conversion risk to AD dementia from normal aging and those with neurodegenerative disorders.
navigation deficits in patients with MCI are associated with a greater risk for developing AD dementia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the study of navigation abilities may provide a valuable tool for the early diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease.
the neural network of spatial navigation is affected by aging and the prodrome of AD in distinct ways, and that these changes can be identified through behavioral and neuroimaging studies.
navigation deficits may be used to identify individuals with MCI at higher risk of conversion to AD.
